survey: A coral cluster on a small pile of rocks on a flat seabed. A large dark purple-grey rock sits in the centre with smaller grey and teal rocks around its base on the left and right. The tall pink branching coral grows up from behind the central rock. Orange corals sit further back on the left and right, and a magenta coral sits in front on the left. A small red fan coral stands on the ground in front of the central rock. The seabed is a flat green band with a horizontal horizon line behind the group. The camera is slightly above the group and looks almost level: the rocks show narrow top faces seen from a little above, and their bottoms rest flat on the seabed with soft contact shadows. The corals are rounded, organic shapes facing the camera, so they have no grid or edge structure that would need to follow a surface. The overlaps read correctly from front to back: red fan coral, then the rocks, then the pink coral, then the orange corals. The two marked ellipses on the red coral's rounded tips (width ratios 0.80 and 0.93) are just rounded bulbs, not rims, and are consistent with a nearly level view. Every part agrees on one low, slightly high camera.
